_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: Apple does publish a Messages framework, so "no API" was wrong. What it is not, is a connector API.

The framework builds app extensions that run inside Messages: an MSMessagesAppViewController presented in the app drawer, with an MSConversation that can insert or send text into the conversation the user is currently looking at. It cannot enumerate conversations, cannot read message history, and cannot act while the user is elsewhere - all three of which are what a connector is for.
It is iOS, iPadOS and macOS only, and it ships as an extension inside an App Store app, not as something a browser can call.

Reading history at all means reading ~/Library/Messages/chat.db on the Mac directly, which is what the reference product does. That needs Full Disk Access, is unsupported by Apple, and does not exist on Windows.
So on this platform there is nothing to connect to. Listed rather than removed, with a badge, because a stated gap is more honest than a quietly shorter list.
Checked against Apple's own framework documentation after the first version of this file claimed Apple published no iMessage API at all. It publishes one; it does not do this job.
